s0201.literal: Thereupon they turned their backs on kindness and broke faith, each setting his own plan; their territory was not like Huainan, yet they harbored an emperor's ambition; their power was not like Yong and Shu, yet they awakened the heart of making themselves kings.
s0201.idiomatic: Thereupon they betrayed kindness and broke faith, each plotting his own course; their lands were no Huainan, yet they nursed an emperor's ambition; their strength was no Yong or Shu, yet they roused the heart of kingship.

s0202.literal: Alas! Since delusion and darkness brought it about, the slaughter and extermination of five clans—fitting indeed!
s0202.idiomatic: Alas—since their own blindness brought it on, the slaughter of five clans was only fitting!

s0204.literal: Exposed at the Vermilion Bird Tower—the Hall edition's textual verification says guan (tower) in the Southern History reads hang (landing).
s0204.idiomatic: On "exposed at the Vermilion Bird Tower": the Hall edition notes tower reads landing in the Southern History.

s0205.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded and was advanced to Pacify-the-South General "Pacify-the-South General"
s0205.idiomatic: On "when Emperor Wen succeeded and was advanced to Pacify-the-South General"

s0208.literal: [Tianchen] year 3 spring "Tianchen" two characters are missing in all editions; now supplied according to the Southern History.
s0208.idiomatic: On "[Tianchen] year 3 spring": Tianchen is missing in all editions and is supplied per the Southern History.

s0209.literal: still split the beast tally "beast" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads tiger.
s0209.idiomatic: On "still split the beast tally": beast in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads tiger.

s0210.literal: Note: this avoids Tang taboo; writing tiger is a later restoration.
s0210.idiomatic: This avoids Tang taboo; tiger is a later restoration.

s0214.literal: Hengzhou Inspector Hou Xiao and others "Hengzhou"
s0214.idiomatic: On "Hengzhou Inspector Hou Xiao and others"

s0216.literal: appended account of Xiao's career reads "East Hengzhou."
s0216.idiomatic: the appended account of Xiao's career reads East Hengzhou.

s0217.literal: enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing county "Yongxing" in the Southern History reads Yongjia.
s0217.idiomatic: On "enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing county": Yongxing in the Southern History reads Yongjia.

s0218.literal: Baoying from the sea route raided Lin'an, Yongjia, and Kuaiji, Yuyao, and Zhuji—Hong Yixuan's Collation of Various Histories says: "Lin'an" should be "Linhai."
s0218.idiomatic: On "Baoying from the sea route raided Lin'an, Yongjia, and Kuaiji, Yuyao, and Zhuji": Hong Yixuan's Collation of Various Histories says Lin'an should be Linhai.

s0219.literal: Note: Linhai with Yongjia, Kuaiji, Yuyao, and Zhuji are all in eastern Zhe; if Lin'an it would be in western Zhe.
s0219.idiomatic: Linhai lies with Yongjia, Kuaiji, Yuyao, and Zhuji in eastern Zhe; Lin'an would be in western Zhe.

s0220.literal: Baoying coming by sea would naturally reach Linhai first; Hong's view is correct.
s0220.idiomatic: Baoying coming by sea would naturally strike Linhai first; Hong is right.

s0221.literal: All these bright shame in teaching battle, Ruxu raising troops—old collation at the chapter end by Zeng Gong and others says "probably in error."
s0221.idiomatic: On "all these bright shame in teaching battle, Ruxu raising troops": old collation at the chapter end by Zeng Gong and others says probably in error.

s0222.literal: Note: this cites the Three Kingdoms Wu Sun Quan's story of drilling troops at Ruxu to resist Cao's army—not in error.
s0222.idiomatic: This cites Sun Quan drilling at Ruxu to resist Cao Cao—not an error.

s0225.literal: "All these bright shame in teaching battle, Ruxu raising troops"—probably in error.
s0225.idiomatic: "All these bright shame in teaching battle, Ruxu raising troops"—probably in error.

s0226.literal: Tongzhou Inspector Li Xie—or the original text reads "Ji La," or "Li Du"—doubtful.
s0226.idiomatic: On "Tongzhou Inspector Li Xie": the original may read Ji La or Li Du—doubtful.

s0227.literal: Xinzhou Inspector Qu Baishou "shou" is the same in all editions; probably should be tiger, also changed to avoid Tang taboo.
s0227.idiomatic: On "Xinzhou Inspector Qu Baishou": shou is the same in all editions; probably should be tiger, likewise a Tang taboo change.

s0228.literal: Former Yuning prefect Ren Mannu "Yuning" in all editions reads Zhang.
s0228.idiomatic: On "former Yuning prefect Ren Mannu": Yuning in all editions reads Zhang.

s0229.literal: Now checking Yuan Gui 216 reads Yuning,

s0231.literal: also reads Yuning, and below there is separately Zhang prefect Liu Guangde—clearly writing Zhang is wrong.
s0231.idiomatic: also reads Yuning, and below there is a separate Zhang prefect Liu Guangde—clearly Zhang is wrong.

s0238.literal: [still] added reward and promotion—emended according to all editions.
s0238.idiomatic: On "[still] added reward and promotion": emended per all editions.
